subject: Cobalt Bio — deployment needs recap and dedicated capacity checklist
messages:
From: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Zhang <emily@cobaltbio.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 03 Apr 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Cobalt Bio kickoff recap + quick checklist for dedicated path

Hi Emily — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and a couple of asks so we can size the Dedicated path cleanly: 

Summary from our side:
- You confirmed the primary workload is real-time document ingestion + question answering for R&D teams, with occasional batch re-embeds.
- Target p95 latency for interactive workflows is ~300ms per request (50–150 tokens typical).
- Expected steady-state TPS: 20 requests/sec during business hours, with peak bursts to 60 TPS for 5–10 minute windows.
- Token mix: about 70% short queries (<=150 tokens), 25% medium (150–800 tokens), 5% long (800–4k tokens).
- Data residency: must remain inside us-west region; private VPC option is nice but Dedicated with strict VPC peering is acceptable.

Immediate asks (attached workbook has same fields):
1) Can you confirm whether clients will batch multiple questions in a single request or always single-turn? (affects KV cache behavior)
2) Do legal/procurement need a separate procurement contact for the Dedicated contract? You referenced a procurement inbox — please confirm.
3) Any restrictions on GPU vendors (NVIDIA A100 vs H100) from your infra team?

Next steps:
- If you confirm single-turn predominance and GPU preference, we’ll circulate a Dedicated SKU recommendation (concurrency, GPU type, expected token-hour estimate) and a basic mutual action plan for a 6-week POC.

Attaching the requirements workbook and our SKU options PDF for your review.

Thanks — talk soon.

Laura Bennett
Senior Account Exec, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0123

Attachments: cobalt_poc_requirements.xlsx (workbook), redwood_dedicated_sku_options.pdf (SKU matrix)

From: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, aditya_rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 03 Apr 2027 18:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Cobalt Bio kickoff recap + quick checklist for dedicated path

Thanks Laura — quick internal readout and notes from the infra POV.

Ben's notes:
- The token mix implies a heavy benefit from KV/prefix caching for short queries; if 70% are <=150 tokens we can aggressively cache and reduce GPU cycles during steady state.
- For peak bursts to 60 TPS, we should size based on sustained 20 TPS but provide headroom via burst pool or autoscale policy. Suggest Dedicated config: 2x H100 or 3x A100 nodes (depending on your price sensitivity). H100 gives better perf on long token cases but is costlier.
- Concurrency: recommend planning for 256 concurrent model contexts across the pool with per-request concurrency throttles to protect latency SLOs.
- Sequence length distribution means we should provision KV cache and token-hour estimates conservatively — I'll attach quick calc (pasted below) to feed into the SKU rec.

Quick calc (rough):
- Steady: 20 TPS * 3600s = 72k req/hour. Average tokens per req ≈ 200 => 14.4M tokens/hour.
- Peak buffer: design for 60 TPS bursts for up to 10 minutes/week — can be served by burst capacity or temporary scaling to 4 nodes.

I'll draft a concise SKU recommendation for Laura to send; want to align with Aditya on quantization tradeoffs (fp16 vs int8) for cost.

Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai

Onward: @aditya — any strong preference on H100 vs A100 for this workload?

From: Emily Zhang <emily@cobaltbio.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@cobaltbio.com
Date: Mon, 05 Apr 2027 08:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Cobalt Bio kickoff recap + quick checklist for dedicated path

Hi Laura — thanks for the clear recap and for the workbook. Answers inline below.

1) Single-turn predominance: confirmed. Our UI issues one QA prompt per user action; we occasionally do multi-question batch jobs but that is <10% of traffic.
2) Procurement contact: yes — please loop procurement@cobaltbio.com on contract and SOW. They will request a security addendum and a standard vendor questionnaire (we included the SOC2 reference in the workbook).
3) GPU vendor restrictions: infra prefers H100s where latency for large context length is critical. If price delta is material we can consider A100 but prefer H100 for the long-tail queries.

Additional notes:
- Data residency: must be in us-west, VPC peering acceptable.
- SLA expectations: 99.9% uptime for dedicated pool during business hours; we will want an escalation path if latency regressions appear.

We'll review the SKU PDF and the workbook now; expect procurement to open a ticket after this thread.

Best,
Emily
Product Ops, Cobalt Bio
emily@cobaltbio.com

2) I'll add procurement@cobaltbio.com to the HubSpot deal and open a procurement checklist item.

4) Attachments: ensure the SKU PDF includes a note about autoscale burst policy to cover 60 TPS short bursts.

Timing: can we have drafts by EOD Wednesday (2027-04-07)? I want to get a quick quote to procurement so they can raise PO.

Thanks team — I'll sync with Emily if any clarifying Qs come up.
